transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Helix CISO), Ravi Shah (Head Infra), Lena Ortiz (Platform Eng), Tom Wu (Product)

Summary: Helix evaluating Redwood for inference across hosted vs dedicated vs private. Primary concerns: SOC 2 and ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs retention and log export, encryption (KMS/HSM) for customer keys, and data retention/residency for regulated datasets. Agreed to share compliance docs and run a technical benchmark.

00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone thanks for taking time, can you hear me okay?
00:06 Maya Thompson: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Alex.
00:10 Alex Kim: Great. So quick agenda — Priya will run through security posture and deployment options, we'll cover SOC2/ISO, SSO and RBAC, audit logging, encryption/KMS, and then Q&A and next steps.
01:02 Priya Patel: Awesome. Hi all, I'm Priya, SE on the infra team. Quick note — we'll talk about three main deployment models: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). We want to map your security reqs to each.
02:05 Ravi Shah: Thanks. From Helix side, we run most regulated workloads in our VPC with Okta SSO, and we need either keys that we manage or a bring-your-own-key model. Also retention for raw genomic data is tricky, 7 years for some datasets.
03:10 Lena Ortiz: Yep and we have strict audit controls — need immutable audit trail, must export logs to our SIEM and also meet internal retention.
03:46 Priya Patel: Totally understood. On SOC 2 and ISO: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate, we can share redacted reports — Alex will drop those links after the call. For Hosted customers we provide attestations and penetration test summaries; for Dedicated and Private we can do in-place audits with your audit team.
05:12 Maya Thompson: When you say "in-place audits" do you mean we can do our own pen test or will Redwood run that?
05:20 Priya Patel: Both, generally. For Private deployments you get full control and can run your pen tests; for Dedicated we often run joint tests — we have a standard process and a list of approved vendors. We'll also provide network diagrams and host-level hardening docs.
06:15 Alex Kim: Also note we support SAML SSO via Okta and can map groups to RBAC roles — engineers vs admin vs billing roles. We support SCIM for provisioning.
07:03 Tom Wu: Is RBAC enforced at the model level? Like can we restrict access to certain models or to inference logs?
07:14 Priya Patel: Yes, policy-level RBAC — you can create roles that only allow read access to logs or call-only access to specific model routes. There's also token scoping so a service token can be limited to embeddings-only, for example.
08:30 Ravi Shah: For encryption — do you offer customer-managed keys? We need keys that we can rotate and audit.
08:38 Jordan Lee: We do. KMS integrations vary by deployment: Hosted supports CMEK via cloud KMS for enterprise tiers — logs show key usage events, but keys remain in your KMS. For Private deployments you can plug in your own HSM/KMS in your VPC. Dedicated can be configured with BYOK on request.
09:20 Maya Thompson: What's the crypto boundary — does Redwood ever have plaintext access to customer data?
09:27 Priya Patel: For Hosted, data is encrypted in transit and at rest; Redwood handles ephemeral plaintext in the serving runtime but access is controlled and logged — no human access to customer plaintext unless in rare incident response with approvals. For Private you control compute so Redwood never touches keys. We'll provide our data flow diagrams.
11:00 Lena Ortiz: Auditing export — can we push logs to our Splunk/Datadog/S3? Need to ingest for e-discovery.
11:12 Priya Patel: Yes, we provide export connectors: streaming audit logs to S3 or Pub/Sub, and Splunk/Datadog integrations. You can configure log retention on your side; Redwood can also retain a copy per your contract, but retention windows are configurable.
12:40 Maya Thompson: Data residency — we need EU-only for some datasets. Does Redwood host in specific regions and can we lock routing?
12:52 Alex Kim: Yes, region pinning is supported. For Hosted accounts you can select region endpoints; Dedicated and Private give you full control of placement. We also support policy-based routing to route EU traffic to EU regions only.
14:05 Ravi Shah: On the dedicated option — if we reserve GPUs, does Redwood handle kernel selection and quantization or do we manage the model bits?
14:20 Priya Patel: Redwood runtime handles kernel selection and quantization for supported model variants. You can pin model versions; on Dedicated we can give you more control and run a customized runtime if needed for compliance.
15:45 Tom Wu: Are there any certification slippage risks with hosted? Like if you need SOC2 evidence quarterly from us?
15:55 Alex Kim: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; updates happen annually and we can push the attestation to customers via a secure portal. For higher assurance we recommend Dedicated or Private if you need continuous audit access.
17:20 Maya Thompson: Ok, what about data retention and deletion — e.g., we need deletion on request and logs tied to user IDs — how long do you keep inference payloads?
17:35 Priya Patel: By default Hosted keeps minimal logs for billing and operational reasons; inference payloads can be configured to be ephemeral or retained for X days depending on contract. We support automatic deletion workflows and can implement retention policies per route. For Dedicated/Private you control retention fully.
19:00 Lena Ortiz: We also need immutable audit trails for privileged actions, and a change log for model deployments.
19:12 Jordan Lee: We have an audit service that records admin actions, deploys, rollouts, and model version changes; entries are signed and exportable. For higher assurance we can time-stamp logs and ship to your S3 bucket.
21:30 Ravi Shah: Network controls — do you support private peering and VPC endpoints? We can't have public egress for some workloads.
21:42 Priya Patel: Yes VPC peering and private endpoints are standard for Private. For Dedicated we offer private connectivity options (direct connect, interconnect) and allow egress controls. Hosted supports IP allowlists and private endpoints for enterprise.
23:05 Maya Thompson: Incident response — SLAs and security event reporting?
23:12 Alex Kim: We have an incident response runbook, 24/7 pager for enterprise customers, and we report security incidents per contract. For Private you can run your own monitoring; for Hosted we push notifications to your security contact and provide post-incident reports.
25:00 Tom Wu: A few specific ask items: sample SOC2 redacted, network diagrams, compliance questionnaire (SIG), and a TCO comparison for Dedicated vs Private.
25:12 Alex Kim: We'll provide those. Priya — you'll attach the TCO and checklist?
25:18 Priya Patel: Yep, I'll send a spreadsheet with assumptions and the deployment checklist.
26:00 Maya Thompson: On legal — do you support data processing addendums and can we get specific language around KMS and key control?
26:10 Alex Kim: Yes DPA and specific BYOK clauses can be added; enterprise legal will handle custom language. We'll loop in our security contact.
27:30 Ravi Shah: One more technical — KV cache persistence, if we run long context prompts, does Redwood persist KV cache between requests?
27:45 Jordan Lee: We do prefix caching and KV cache improvements; cache persistence is configurable. For privacy you can disable persistent caching, or we can only cache within a session. We'll show benchmark results in the tech run.
29:00 Lena Ortiz: For the benchmark — we'd like to test latency at 1k QPS and tail latencies, and also verify encryption overhead.
29:08 Priya Patel: That sounds good — we'll propose a benchmark plan and required sample payloads.
31:15 Maya Thompson: Any references to third-party auditors or penetration test results?
31:22 Alex Kim: Yes, we have a list of third-party pen testers and can share recent summaries. We'll redact sensitive details but provide severity and remediation status.
33:10 Tom Wu: Competitor question — we've also looked at Anthropic and building internally; how does Redwood compare on auditability?
33:22 Alex Kim: On auditability Redwood focuses on production controls and observability — per-token tracing, audit logs, and export hooks. If you self-host you get more control but more ops. Compared to cloud vendors we provide more inference-focused telemetry.
35:30 Maya Thompson: Ok budget and timeline — we hope to decide by end of Q2, pilot in Q3. Security review is gating.
35:38 Alex Kim: That's reasonable. We'll prioritize sending the SOC2 pack and TCO.
37:00 Ravi Shah: For the Private deployment, what's the expected lead time?
37:08 Priya Patel: Private deployments vary — for a VPC-hosted Private it's typically 6-10 weeks end-to-end depending on networking approvals; Dedicated is faster if we use our reserved pools, usually 2-4 weeks once contracts are signed.
38:40 Lena Ortiz: Are we able to get a short-term dedicated environment for bench testing while legal completes DPA?
38:49 Alex Kim: Yes, we can provide a temporary sandbox Dedicated environment for benchmark runs under our eval agreement. We'll scope the limits.
40:10 Maya Thompson: Great. Last Q — do you offer HIPAA BAAs, since some of our datasets are PHI?
40:20 Priya Patel: We support HIPAA for enterprise customers and can execute a BAA; generally Dedicated or Private is recommended for PHI. We'll include our compliance summary.
41:05 Alex Kim: Thanks everyone — recap in the notes, we'll send SOC2, ISO, TCO spreadsheet, schedule the benchmark for w/c 2026-03-23. Any final items?
41:20 Maya Thompson: No, that's it. Thanks.
41:30 End of recording.
